subject: please help me understand how coloring works with geom = "point"

messages.author: 393a7437f3070ac9
messages.subject: please help me understand how coloring works with geom = "point"
parts:
I am trying to get each point to be colored according to a pallet
defined by me, similar to how tile coloring works.

The following results in a very predictable color code for the tiles.

col <- c("red", "green", "blue", "purple", "orange", "yellow", "cyan",
"black", "brown", "grey")
qplot(1:10, 1:10, fill = col, geom = "tile") + scale_fill_identity()

However, if the geom is changed to "point", it does not color
appropriately. Points get their coloring independent of the fill
parameter, I guess.

col <- c("red", "green", "blue", "purple", "orange", "yellow", "cyan",
"black", "brown", "grey")
qplot(1:10, 1:10, fill = col, geom = "point") + scale_fill_identity()

If I add a colour parameter, they get colored, but not the way I would
predict based on the vector of colors I assign.

col <- c("red", "green", "blue", "purple", "orange", "yellow", "cyan",
"black", "brown", "grey")
qplot(1:10, 1:10, colour = col, geom = "point") +
scale_fill_identity()

qplot(1:10, 1:10, fill= col, colour = col, geom = "point") +
scale_fill_identity()

Is there a way to get the point geom to adher to the assigned color or
does it have to choose its own color randomly from a hat? I just want
the points to be the colors I assign.
Thanks,
Tim

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: please help me understand how coloring works with geom = "point"
parts:
Hi,

try this:

qplot(1:10, 1:10, colour = col, geom = "point") + scale_colour_identity()
